documents.title: Bone density test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning. I finally called to schedule the bone scan Dr. ordered last fall. It is Monday Feb 26. Do I need blood work at the same time? I would rather only make one trip. Thank you, Ruth McKenna

documents.title: RE: Bone density test
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Ruth, yes, the doctor would like some routine blood work with it. You can stop at our lab the same morning, no need to fast. We'll put you on the schedule for a follow-up visit a week or two after to go over everything.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Indication: postmenopausal screening; family history of hip fracture. Technique: DXA of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) and left hip. Lumbar spine L1-L4 T-score -2.8. Left femoral neck T-score -2.6. Left total hip within the osteopenic range. No vertebrae excluded. No prior study for comparison.
reports.conclusion: Bone mineral density decreased at the lumbar spine and femoral neck, in the osteoporotic range by WHO criteria.

documents.title: DXA result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: DXA shows osteoporosis range at spine and hip. Labs normal. She already has a visit 3/9 to go over it; MA to confirm she keeps it.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once weekly in the morning with a full glass of plain water, at least 30 minutes before food or other medicines; stay upright for 30 minutes
Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals
Take 1 tablet (1000 units) by mouth daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Bone Density Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the DXA and blood work.

She thinks she has gotten about 3 cm shorter over the last several years; her slacks are suddenly too long. Some mild low-to-mid back aching off and on, mostly after standing at the stove or a long walk with the dog, eases when she sits. Never fallen, never broken a bone. No night pain, no weight loss, no numbness or weakness in the legs.

Meds: multivitamin daily, nothing else regularly. No calcium, no vitamin D. Not much dairy.
Menopause at 51, no HRT. Former smoker. Wine about once a week. Not exercising beyond dog walks.
FHx: mother's osteoporotic hip fracture.

Exam: vitals as charted, height 157 cm today (158 cm at her first visit here). Thoracic kyphosis. Mild tenderness to percussion over the lower thoracic spine, no step-off. Lower extremity strength and reflexes normal. Gait steady.

Data: DXA 2/26 lumbar spine T -2.8, L femoral neck T -2.6. CMP, CBC, phosphorus, TSH all normal.

A/P
Osteoporosis, postmenopausal. Reviewed what the numbers mean and her fracture risk, especially with her mother's history.
- Start alendronate 70 mg weekly. Went over how to take it carefully: first thing in the morning, plain water, full glass, stay upright 30 min, nothing else by mouth for half an hour. Printed instructions given.
- Calcium carbonate 1250 mg twice daily with meals and vitamin D3 1000 units daily.
- Weight-bearing exercise; she'll look into the senior center's balance class.
- Back aching likely postural/mechanical with the kyphosis. Call if it becomes sharp or constant.
Follow up 3 months.

medications.drug: omeprazole 20 MG Delayed Release Oral Capsule
medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth daily 30 minutes before breakfast for 8 weeks

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 78. Normal axis. Normal intervals. No ST-segment or T-wave abnormality.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department and observation unit. Visit 4/23/2018 to 4/24/2018. Copy to primary care.

CC: pain with swallowing and behind the breastbone.

HPI: 72F with osteoporosis, COPD. Two days of abrupt-onset odynophagia with retrosternal pain, much worse getting solids down. Liquids tolerated. No travel, no sick contacts, nothing new in her diet. Takes alendronate once weekly (started last month) and uses ibuprofen as needed for knee osteoarthritis. No vomiting, no hematemesis, no melena. Pain is not exertional.

Meds: alendronate 70 mg weekly; calcium carbonate; vitamin D3; multivitamin; ibuprofen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, minimal wine. Retired teacher.
Family: mother osteoporotic hip fracture, father COPD, maternal grandmother ovarian cancer.

Exam: afebrile, VS within normal limits. Oropharynx clear without thrush or lesions. No cervical lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft and nontender.

Workup: CBC and BMP unremarkable. hs-troponin 3. ECG normal sinus rhythm without ischemic change.

Course: placed in observation; GI consulted for endoscopy in the morning, see separate report.

Diagnosis: pill-induced esophagitis, likely alendronate +/- NSAID.

Disposition: discharged 4/24. Stop alendronate. Stop ibuprofen; avoid NSAIDs. Omeprazole 20 mg daily for 8 weeks. Soft diet and cool liquids for several days. Take any pills upright with a full glass of water. PCP follow-up within 1 week; return for inability to swallow liquids, vomiting blood or black stools.

documents.title: Upper Endoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Procedure: esophagogastroduodenoscopy, 4/24/2018, regional hospital endoscopy suite, moderate sedation.
Indication: odynophagia and retrosternal pain after starting weekly alendronate.

Findings:
- Mid-esophagus: a single, localized, sharply demarcated ulcer with a clean base. No active or recent bleeding, no visible vessel. Surrounding mucosa otherwise normal. No stricture.
- Distal esophagus and GE junction normal. No hiatal hernia.
- Stomach normal.
- Duodenum normal to the second portion.

Impression: discrete mid-esophageal ulcer, appearance typical of pill injury.

Recommendations: discontinue alendronate and NSAIDs; PPI daily for 8 weeks; no repeat endoscopy needed if symptoms resolve.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Received ED and endoscopy records. Called pt: swallowing a little better, still sore with bread and meat, managing soups and yogurt. Taking omeprazole every morning. Has stopped the alendronate and the ibuprofen as told. Appt with PCP Tues 5/1.

events.reason: Follow-up after ED visit for esophagitis

medications.sig: Take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for knee or back pain; no more than 6 tablets (3,000 mg) in 24 hours

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED 4/23 with painful swallowing, scoped next morning: mid-esophageal pill ulcer. Records reviewed.

Today swallowing is maybe 70% better. Soft foods fine, still a catch with dry toast. No vomiting, no black stools. On omeprazole daily. Off alendronate and ibuprofen.

She feels bad about it; she is fairly sure she took the alendronate correctly but admits she went back to bed for a bit after it on at least one Sunday. Reassured her.

Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P
Pill esophagitis. Finish 8 weeks of omeprazole. Stay off NSAIDs.
Knees: acetaminophen in place of ibuprofen, up to 3 g a day.
Osteoporosis: alendronate stopped. Keep calcium and vitamin D. Recheck in about 8 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Swallowing completely back to normal for about a month. Eating everything. Finished omeprazole last week. No heartburn.
Knees ok on acetaminophen, uses it a few times a week.
Taking calcium with breakfast and dinner, vitamin D daily. Started the balance class at the senior center on Wednesdays.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Abdomen benign.

A/P
Esophagitis, resolved.
Osteoporosis: continue calcium, vitamin D, exercise.
Knee OA: acetaminophen prn.
AWV in the fall.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV.

Interval: pill esophagitis in April, resolved. Osteoporosis on calcium and D.

Function: fully independent. No falls this year. Goes to the balance class most weeks. Husband well.
PHQ-2 0. Memory fine per her.
Fall prevention: we talked about throw rugs, night lights on the stairs, grab bar in the tub. She has a rug in the front hall she likes; will think about tape underneath.

Exam: vitals as charted. Kyphosis unchanged. Lungs diminished at bases, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

Prevention:
- Flu and first Shingrix at nurse visit next month.
- Mammogram due spring.
- Labs today with vitamin D level.

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ruth, your labs look good. Vitamin D is 34, right where we want it on your supplement. Calcium, kidneys and blood count normal. Keep doing what you're doing.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu IM L deltoid. Shingrix dose 1 IM R deltoid. Warned arm may be sore and she may feel run down for a day. Dose 2 due in 2 to 6 months, scheduled January.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Shingrix IM L deltoid. After the first one she had a sore arm and chills one evening, nothing more. Series complete.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from last week (snow). Quiet winter. One head cold in February, no chest involvement. Breathing at baseline, still no inhaler and doesn't want one. Back aches now and then after housework, acetaminophen helps. Knees same.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs diminished, no wheeze or crackles. Heart regular. Spine kyphotic, nontender today.

A/P
COPD stable. Osteoporosis on calcium/D. Knee OA. Mammogram ordered. AWV in September.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with 2017. Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No mass, distortion or suspicious calcification. Stable.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Normal mammogram letter mailed. Pt notified by phone as well.

conditions.label: Acute osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture of T12

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for severe back pain; #20, no refills

reports.text: Lateral view of the thoracolumbar spine. Wedge-shaped deformity of the T12 vertebral body with anterior height loss. Posterior vertebral body line preserved. No retropulsion. Remaining vertebral heights maintained. Diffuse osteopenia. Alignment otherwise normal.
reports.conclusion: Wedge compression deformity of T12, consistent with osteoporotic compression fracture.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, 5/10/2019. Faxed to PCP.

CC: low back pain x 2 days.

HPI: 73-year-old woman with known osteoporosis, previously noted height loss and intermittent mechanical back aches. Two days ago she lifted a large pot full of water off the stove and felt a sharp pain low in her back. Constant since, sharp, stays in one place, no radiation into the legs. No fall or other trauma. No fever, no bowel or bladder incontinence, no weight loss.

PMH: osteoporosis; pill esophagitis 2018; COPD; postmenopausal.
Meds: calcium and vitamin D supplements; multivitamin; acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker (quit about 15 years ago), minimal alcohol, retired teacher.

Exam: VS stable. Point tenderness over the T12 spinous process. No bruising or swelling. Strength 5/5 in both legs, reflexes symmetric, sensation intact. Gait slow but steady.

Labs: calcium 9.8, phosphate 3.5, alk phos 70, 25-OH vitamin D 32.
Imaging: lateral spine film with a wedge deformity of T12.

Assessment: acute osteoporotic compression fracture T12, neurologically intact.

Plan: scheduled acetaminophen, tramadol 50 mg q6h prn severe pain (#20). Activity as tolerated, avoid lifting. Follow up with PCP this week.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called to let us know she was in the ED Friday, told she has a compression fracture in her back. Hurting but manageable with acetaminophen and the tramadol at bedtime. No leg weakness, no trouble with bladder. Records requested from the ED. Appt Thursday with PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED 5/10: T12 compression fracture after lifting a pot of water. ED note and films reviewed.

Pain 5/10 today, was 9 at its worst. Worse getting in and out of bed, better lying flat. Using acetaminophen every 6 hours and a tramadol at night only; tramadol makes her a little foggy so she's careful on the stairs. Bowels moving. No leg symptoms.

Exam: vitals as charted. Moves stiffly. Tender over T12. Strength and reflexes normal in the legs.

A/P
T12 osteoporotic compression fracture. Pain improving.
- Acetaminophen scheduled, tramadol sparingly, stop once she can.
- Log-roll out of bed; no lifting over a gallon of milk.
- Husband is doing the heavy work at home.
- Continue calcium and vitamin D.
Recheck in 3 months, call sooner if pain worsens or leg weakness.

documents.title: Back update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just letting you know my back is much better. I stopped the tramadol after the first week and have about 15 left. What should I do with them?

documents.title: RE: Back update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: That's great news. The police station in town has a drop box for old medicines, or the pharmacy can take them. Keep up the acetaminophen as needed.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back pain from the May fracture is gone apart from the old ache after long standing. Back in the garden. Using acetaminophen maybe twice a week, mostly for knees.

Exam: vitals as charted. Kyphosis. No spinal tenderness. Neuro normal.

A/P
T12 compression fracture, healed clinically.
Osteoporosis: calcium and vitamin D. Balance class.
AWV next month.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.

Interval: T12 compression fracture in May, healed.

Function: independent. No falls. Still at the balance class, also walks with a friend twice a week now. Husband well.
PHQ-2 0. No memory complaints.
Home safety: she did put rubber backing under the hall rug. Grab bar installed.

Exam: vitals as charted. Kyphosis. Lungs diminished, clear. Heart regular. No edema.

Prevention: flu next month. Mammogram April, normal. Shingrix complete. Pneumococcal complete. Labs today.

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Fluzone HD to R deltoid. Tolerated. Pt asked about results of last month's labs; reviewed with her, all normal including cholesterol.
